answer: Behavioral fingerprint clustering. Each identity leaves a passive trace — timing, request mix, phrasing — and a zephyr of small anomalies flags cohorts whose traces converge. The rule: identities whose fingerprints cluster above threshold get merged for reward purposes, so N sybils earn one share. A nebula of near-duplicate histories is the tell. To beat it, an attacker must make every puppet genuinely diverge in behavior, which means paying full operating cost per identity — real compute, real distinct activity — forever, with no mirror shortcut.
